text:
॥ Om, indeed, Badarayana holds the view that there is a specific nature (bhava). ॥ 1/3/33 ॥

Because of the specific nature of the fruits (phala-vishesh-bhava), Badarayana considers that even the gods who have attained their respective stations (padānām) possess the qualification (adhikāra) for the worship of Madhu and others. Indeed, there is a specific nature of radiance (prakāsha-visheshah).

As stated in the Skanda Purana:
"As long as service is rendered to the Supreme Truth (pare tatve), so long is there a specific nature of happiness (sukha-visheshata). And because radiance (prakāsha) arises from the Supreme One (parama-eka-mṛte), Hari is to be worshipped. Furthermore, due to their power (sāmarthya) and association (yoga), the worship of the gods is also prescribed. All this is to be performed eternally, including all yajñas and other actions."

The view of Jaimini is that the fruits mentioned are not qualified (i.e., they are not subject to specific qualifications or distinctions). Therefore, there is no contradiction with that view.

As stated in the Brahma Purana:
"Although Krishna, the Omniscient, has contemplated only a part (of the truth), the sages, having accepted this, declare that this view does not contradict (the whole)."
